name: Sheet masking

card.summary: Applying a single-use fabric or paper sheet soaked in serum to the face, a routine used to hydrate the skin and give it a smoother, plumper look.
card.note: Long wear times may irritate skin.

quick.overview:
A sheet mask is a piece of paper, cellulose or fabric, pre-soaked in a serum or essence, that is laid on the face for a set time. Users apply them in series or as a regular routine for a hydrated, smoother and brighter-looking complexion.

The look comes from the mask holding the serum against the skin, which increases surface moisture. Controlled studies have measured skin moisture and water loss with different mask types, and a collagen sheet mask has been evaluated in a clinical study for skin health and appearance.
quick.how: People cleanse, apply the mask for the time the packet suggests (often about 15 to 20 minutes), remove it and pat in leftover essence. Some do several in a week, or a themed series (hydrating, brightening, soothing). Mask types include pure water, hyaluronan, collagen and ferment-lysate formulas.
quick.risks: A randomised trial examined skin reactions across wear durations of 5 to 40 minutes and noted that prolonged use may cause skin inflammation. Preservatives such as phenoxyethanol and methylparaben have been measured in exposure studies. Those with sensitive or rosacea-prone skin sometimes react to ingredients.

lead: A sheet mask is a piece of paper, cellulose or fabric used to apply a facial mask, according to Wikipedia; the sheet is soaked in a liquid formulation and worn for a short period [3]. People use them to hydrate the skin and improve its smoothness, glow and plumpness.

The global facial mask market is reported to grow around 8.5% per year [2]. Randomised trials have investigated how mask type and wear time affect skin physiology: a 2024 trial compared pure water, hyaluronan and bifida ferment lysate masks at four durations and measured moisture, water loss and aquaporin-3 expression [2]. A 2024 study of a native bovine collagen sheet mask evaluated skin health and appearance [4].

A 2022 randomised study of 175 Chinese adults examined how much product is actually transferred per application, as a basis for safety assessment of ingredients such as phenoxyethanol and methylparaben [1].

angle.text: The sheet keeps a hydrating formula in contact with the skin, which temporarily increases surface moisture and gives a smoother, plumper look. Users repeat the masks in series or a weekly routine.

paras: The sheet is made from polymers or fibre and is pre-soaked. Wikipedia notes research into bio-based and biodegradable materials such as polysaccharides and pullulan, and into designs that may improve delivery of actives [3]. Other formats include gel masks, and researchers have developed nanofibrous medicated sheets, for example a spironolactone-loaded sheet studied in rosacea models [5].

The 2024 randomised trial measured moisture content, transepidermal water loss and AQP3 across mask types and durations, noting prolonged wear may inflame skin [2]. The collagen sheet mask study evaluated skin health and appearance outcomes [4].

The exposure study measured how much preservative reaches the skin per mask, with the aim of informing risk assessment [1]. The duration trial indicates that wearing beyond the intended time was associated with skin reactions [2].

Human trials include the exposure study (n=175) [1], the randomised wear-time and mask-type trial [2] and the collagen sheet mask evaluation [4]. A rosacea-oriented medicated mask has been tested in preclinical work [5].
